message.content:
In Blackjack, an Ace is a “flexible” card: it can be counted as either **1** or **11**, depending on which value gives your hand the best chance of winning without busting.

Key points:

| Situation | How the Ace is treated |
|-----------|------------------------|
| **Single Ace + other cards** | Count as 11 unless that would make the total exceed 21; then count as 1. |
| **Two Aces** | One Ace counts as 11, the other as 1, giving a total of 12. |
| **Natural Blackjack** | An Ace plus a 10‑value card (10, J, Q, K) totals 21 on the first two cards – this is called a “blackjack” and usually pays 3:2. |
| **Splitting Aces** | If you’re dealt two Aces, you may split them into two separate hands. Most rules let you hit each new hand once (you can’t hit again after splitting Aces). |
| **Soft Hand** | Any hand containing an Ace counted as 11 is called a “soft” hand (e.g., Ace‑6 = soft 17). Soft hands can be hit safely because the Ace can switch to 1 if needed. |

So, the core rule: **An Ace can be worth 1 or 11, whichever keeps the hand’s total at or below 21 and maximizes its value.**
